record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.context_brief: Two-machine open shop with proportional operations
record.original_question: Given a two-machine open shop in which each job has one operation on each machine and operation i of job j has proportional time-dependent processing time p_ij(t) = b_ij t when it starts at time t, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this two-machine open-shop time-dependent scheduling problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or can it be solved in polynomial time?

evidence.quote: O 2|p ij =b ij t|P C j

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-machine open shop scheduling problem defined as follows. There are n jobs and two machines M_1, M_2. Each job j (1 ≤ j ≤ n) consists of two operations: operation (1,j) must be processed on M_1 and operation (2,j) must be processed on M_2; the two operations of a job may be processed in any order but not simultaneously, and each machine processes at most one operation at a time. Processing times are proportional and time-dependent: if operation (i,j) starts at time t ≥ 0, its processing time is p_{ij}(t) = b_{ij} · t, where b_{ij} > 0 is a given rate (assume a common starting time t_0 > 0, so processing times are well-defined and positive). Let C_j denote the completion time of job j in a feasible schedule. The objective is to minimize the total completion time Σ_{j=1}^{n} C_j.

Determine the computational complexity of this problem. Specifically, decide whether the problem is NP-hard (in the ordinary sense or strongly) or whether it admits a polynomial-time algorithm.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not locate a published complexity result settling this specific problem (two-machine open shop with proportional time-dependent processing times p_{ij}(t) = b_{ij} t under the total completion time objective). Related results exist for the makespan objective (polynomial-time solvable for the two-machine open shop with proportional/simple linear deterioration, due to Mosheiov) and for three-machine open shops with simple linear deterioration (ordinary NP-hard), but the two-machine open shop case with the Σ C_j objective and proportional processing times appears to remain unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Proportionate and Ordered Open Shops
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of job-proportionate and machine-proportionate open shops noting equivalence for makespan but not for other objective functions.
status_evidence.claim: Two-machine open shop proportional variants are studied mainly for makespan; behavior under other objectives differs and is less settled.

status_evidence.title: Literature Review of Open Shop Scheduling Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open shop scheduling complexity results.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys do not list a definitive polynomial algorithm or NP-hardness proof for the two-machine open shop with proportional time-dependent processing and total completion time objective.
